sentences.zh: 謝尚

translations.literal: Xie Shang.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Shang

sentences.zh: 謝尚，字仁祖，豫章太守鯤之子也。

translations.literal: Xie Shang, courtesy name Renzu, was a son of Xie Kun, the Administrator of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Shang, whose courtesy name was Renzu, was the son of Xie Kun, governor of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 幼有至性。

translations.literal: In childhood he had utmost natural disposition.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a child he showed exceptional native goodness.

sentences.zh: 七歲喪兄，哀慟過禮，親戚異之。

translations.literal: At seven he lost an elder brother; his grief and mourning exceeded the rites, and relatives considered him extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: When he was seven his elder brother died; he grieved so deeply that he outstripped what ritual prescribed, and kinsmen marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 八歲神悟夙成。

translations.literal: At eight his spiritual insight and comprehension were precociously complete.
translations.idiomatic: By eight his intuition and understanding were already remarkably mature.

sentences.zh: 鯤嘗攜之送客，或曰：「此兒一坐之顏回也。

translations.literal: Kun once took him along when seeing off a guest; someone said: “This boy is a Yan Hui for the whole seated company.”
translations.idiomatic: Once, when Kun brought him along to see a guest off, someone remarked, “For everyone at this mat, the boy is another Yan Hui.”

sentences.zh: 」尚應聲答曰：「坐無尼父，焉別顏回！

translations.literal: Shang answered on the spur of the moment: “If in the seat there is no Confucius, how can one distinguish a Yan Hui!”
translations.idiomatic: Shang shot back, “With no Confucius at the mat, who could pick out a Yan Hui?”

sentences.zh: 」席賓莫不歎異。

translations.literal: The guests at the mat none failed to sigh in wonder.
translations.idiomatic: Every guest at the gathering murmured in admiration.

sentences.zh: 十餘歲，遭父憂，丹陽尹溫嶠吊之，尚號咷極哀。

translations.literal: In his teens he encountered his father’s bereavement; Wen Jiao, the Prefect of Danyang, came to condole, and Shang wailed with extreme grief.
translations.idiomatic: Before he was twenty his father died; Wen Jiao, prefect of Danyang, called to offer condolences, and Shang gave way to violent weeping.

sentences.zh: 既而收涕告訴，舉止有異常童，嶠甚奇之。

translations.literal: Presently he swallowed his tears and stated his grievance; his bearing was unlike an ordinary child, and Jiao greatly marveled.
translations.idiomatic: Then he dried his tears and poured out his sorrow; his composure was unlike any ordinary boy’s, and Jiao was deeply struck.

sentences.zh: 及長，開率穎秀，辨悟絕倫，脫略細行，不為流俗之事。

translations.literal: When grown, he was open, frank, and outstandingly talented; his discernment and intuitive grasp were unequaled; he sloughed off petty conduct and did not do what vulgar fashion did.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he was candid and brilliant, with judgment and insight few could match; he brushed aside small-minded scruples and refused the petty pursuits of the crowd.

sentences.zh: 好衣刺文袴，諸父責之，而因自改，遂知名。

translations.literal: He liked to wear embroidered trousers; his uncles reproved him, and he therefore reformed himself, and thus became known.
translations.idiomatic: He favored brocaded breeches until his uncles scolded him; he mended his ways of his own accord and so earned a reputation.

sentences.zh: 善音樂，博綜眾藝。

translations.literal: He was skilled in music and broadly combined many arts.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at music and commanded a wide range of accomplishments.

sentences.zh: 司徒王導深器之，比之王戎，常呼為「小安豐」，辟為掾。

translations.literal: Wang Dao, the Minister of Education, deeply valued him, compared him to Wang Rong, regularly called him “Young Anfeng,” and summoned him as a clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Education Wang Dao thought the world of him, likened him to Wang Rong, habitually called him “little Anfeng,” and appointed him to his staff.

sentences.zh: 襲父爵咸亭侯。

translations.literal: He inherited his father’s noble rank as Marquis of Xianting.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeded to his father’s title as marquis of Xianting.

sentences.zh: 始到府通謁，導以其有勝會，謂曰：「聞君能作鴝鵒舞，一坐傾想，寧有此理不？

translations.literal: When he first arrived at the office to pay respects, Dao, because there was an excellent gathering, said to him: “I hear you can perform the mynah-bird dance—the whole seat leans toward the thought; can there really be such a thing?”
translations.idiomatic: On his first visit to the ministry, Dao—knowing a choice company was assembled—said, “They say you can dance the mynah dance; everyone here is dying to see it. Can it be true?”

sentences.zh: 」尚曰：「佳。

translations.literal: Shang said: “Good.”
translations.idiomatic: Shang replied, “Gladly.”

sentences.zh: 」便著衣幘而舞，導令坐者撫掌擊節，尚俯仰在中，傍若無人，其率詣如此。

translations.literal: He then put on robes and cap and danced; Dao ordered those seated to clap hands and beat time; Shang bent and straightened among them as if no one else were there—such was his forthrightness.
translations.idiomatic: He donned formal dress and cap and danced while Dao had the company clap and keep time; Shang swayed through the steps as though the room were empty—so unguarded was his manner.

sentences.zh: 轉西曹屬，時有遭亂與父母乖離，議者或以進仕理王事，婚姻繼百世，於理非嫌。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be a subordinate of the Western Bureau; at that time some who had suffered turmoil were separated from their parents; debaters held that advancing to office to order the king’s business and marriage to continue a hundred generations were not objectionable in principle.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to a post in the Western Bureau, he found men arguing that those torn from their parents by war might still take office for the state and marry to perpetuate their line without moral fault.

sentences.zh: 尚議曰：「典禮之興，皆因循情理，開通弘勝。

translations.literal: Shang argued: “The rise of canonical ritual always follows human feeling and reason, opening the way to broad excellence.”
translations.idiomatic: Shang countered, “Ritual grows out of human feeling and right principle; it should widen our humanity, not choke it.”

sentences.zh: 如運有屯夷，要當斷之以大義。

translations.literal: “If fortune brings obstruction and calamity, one must in any case decide by great principle.”
translations.idiomatic: “When fate turns cruel, judgment must still rest on the greater moral law.”

sentences.zh: 夫無後之罪，三千所不過，今婚姻將以繼百世，崇宗緒，此固不可塞也。

translations.literal: “The offense of having no heir is not among the three thousand [faults the Zhou code did not punish]; now marriage is to continue a hundred generations and exalt the clan line—this indeed must not be blocked off.”
translations.idiomatic: “Failing to produce an heir was never counted among the gravest crimes; marriage exists to carry the hundred generations forward and honor the ancestral thread—that door cannot be shut.”

sentences.zh: 然至於天屬生離之哀，父子乖絕之痛，痛之深者，莫深於茲。

translations.literal: “Yet as for the sorrow of heaven-sent kin torn alive apart, the pain of father and son cruelly severed—among deep pains none is deeper than this.”
translations.idiomatic: “Yet nothing cuts deeper than the grief of kin torn apart while still living, of father and son cruelly separated.”

sentences.zh: 夫以一體之小患，猶或忘思慮，損聽察，況於抱傷心之巨痛，懷忉恆之至戚，方寸既亂，豈能綜理時務哉！

translations.literal: “For a small ailment of one body we may still lose thought and hearing; how much more, embracing a wound of the heart and hugging utmost grief and sorrow—the mind in turmoil—how could one then manage the affairs of the age!”
translations.idiomatic: “A minor bodily illness can cloud thought and dull the senses; how then can someone crushed by heartbreak and endless mourning, his inner world in chaos, hope to govern the realm?”

sentences.zh: 有心之人，決不冒榮苟進。

translations.literal: “A person of real mind will never court glory and advance improperly.”
translations.idiomatic: “Anyone with a conscience will refuse rank seized in haste and bad faith.”

sentences.zh: 冒榮苟進之疇，必非所求之旨，徒開偷薄之門而長流弊之路。

translations.literal: “The sort who court glory and improper advancement cannot be what we seek in principle; they only open the gate to callous frivolity and lengthen the road of floating abuse.”
translations.idiomatic: “Such climbers are not the men we want; they only invite cynicism and entrench corruption.”

sentences.zh: 或有執志丘園、守心不革者，猶當崇其操業以弘風尚，而況含艱履戚之人，勉之以榮貴邪？」

translations.literal: “Some who keep their resolve in hills and gardens and do not change their heart—we should still honor their conduct to enlarge the tone of society; how much less should men who bear hardship and tread in grief be urged toward rank and honor?”
translations.idiomatic: “Even recluses who never waver deserve respect for holding the moral high ground—how much less should we prod the grief-stricken toward titles and wealth?”

sentences.zh: 遷會稽王友，入補給事黃門侍郎，出為建武將軍、曆陽太守，轉督江夏義陽隨三郡軍事、江夏相，將軍如故。

translations.literal: He was promoted to be a companion to the Prince of Kuaiji, entered to fill the post of Palace Attendant of the Yellow Gate, went out as General Who Establishes Might and Prefect of Liyang, then was transferred to supervise the military affairs of the three commands Jiangxia, Yiyang, and Sui and to serve as Chancellor of Jiangxia, while remaining General as before.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to companion to the Prince of Kuaiji, then served at court as a Yellow Gate palace attendant before taking the field as General Who Establishes Might and prefect of Liyang; later he commanded the armies of Jiangxia, Yiyang, and Sui while serving as Jiangxia’s chancellor, keeping his general’s commission.

sentences.zh: 時安西將軍庾翼鎮武昌，尚數詣翼咨謀軍事。

translations.literal: At that time Yu Yi, the General Who Guards the West, was stationed at Wuchang; Shang several times visited Yi to consult on military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yi, General Who Guards the West, held Wuchang, and Shang often rode over to discuss strategy with him.

sentences.zh: 嘗與翼共射，翼曰：「卿若破的，當以鼓吹相賞。

translations.literal: He once shot targets with Yi; Yi said: “If you can hit the bull’s-eye, I shall reward you with a wind-and-drum band.”
translations.idiomatic: Once they shot together; Yi said, “Break the target and the military band is yours.”

sentences.zh: 」尚應聲中之，翼即以其副鼓吹給之。

translations.literal: Shang as soon as the words were spoken hit the mark; Yi at once gave him his deputy band.
translations.idiomatic: Shang loosed an arrow the instant Yi finished speaking and struck true; Yi handed over his secondary band on the spot.

sentences.zh: 尚為政清簡，始到官，郡府以布四十匹為尚造烏布帳。

translations.literal: Shang governed in a clear, simple manner; when he first took office, the commandery and his headquarters had forty bolts of cloth made into a black cloth canopy for Shang.
translations.idiomatic: Shang ruled with austere simplicity; on arriving, he found the yamen had requisitioned forty bolts of cloth to sew him a black cloth canopy.

sentences.zh: 尚壞之，以為軍士褚襦袴。

translations.literal: Shang destroyed it and used it for soldiers’ padded undershirts and trousers.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered it torn down and had the fabric cut into padded jackets and trousers for his troops.

sentences.zh: 建元二年，詔曰：「尚往以戎戍事要，故輟黃散，以授軍旅。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianyuan, an edict said: “Formerly, because military duty on the frontier was pressing, Shang was therefore removed from the Yellow Gate attendant post and assigned to the army.”
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyuan 2 an edict read: “Because frontier duty was urgent, Shang was earlier stripped of his Yellow Gate post and placed under arms.”

sentences.zh: 所處險要，宜崇其威望。

translations.literal: “The place he holds is strategically crucial; his prestige and authority should be enhanced.”
translations.idiomatic: “His position is strategically vital; his prestige must be heightened.”

sentences.zh: 今以為南中郎將，餘官如故。

translations.literal: “Now we appoint him General of the Centre of the South; his other offices remain as before.”
translations.idiomatic: “He is now named General of the Centre of the South; all other titles stand.”

sentences.zh: 」會庾冰薨，復以本號督豫州四郡，領江州刺史。

translations.literal: When Yu Bing died, he was again given his former title to supervise the four commands of Yuzhou and to hold the governorship of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Bing soon died, and Shang resumed his old rank to oversee four Yuzhou commands while governing Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 俄而復轉西中郎將、督揚州之六郡諸軍事、豫州刺史、假節，鎮曆陽。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was again transferred to General of the Centre of the West, to supervise the military affairs of the six commanderies of Yangzhou, to be Governor of Yuzhou, to hold the credential staff, and to be stationed at Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he shifted to General of the Centre of the West, took command of six Yangzhou commanderies, became governor of Yuzhou, received the ceremonial baton, and garrisoned Liyang.

sentences.zh: 大司馬桓溫欲有事中原，使尚率眾向壽春，進號安西將軍。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Huan Wen wished to undertake operations in the Central Plains and ordered Shang to lead the host toward Shouchun; Shang was advanced in rank to General Who Guards the West.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Huan Wen planned a push into the heartland and sent Shang toward Shouyang with the main force, promoting him to General Who Guards the West.

sentences.zh: 初，苻健將張遇降尚，尚不能綏懷之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhang Yu, a general of Fu Jian, had surrendered to Shang; Shang was unable to console and win him over.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yu, once a general under Fu Jian, had defected to Shang, but Shang failed to reassure him.

sentences.zh: 遇怒，據許昌叛。

translations.literal: Yu in anger rebelled, seizing Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Zhang Yu seized Xuchang and rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 尚討之，為遇所敗，收付廷尉。

translations.literal: Shang campaigned against him, was defeated by Yu, was taken into custody and handed to the Court Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Shang marched against him, lost, and was arrested and remanded to the minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 時康獻皇后臨朝，即尚之甥也，特令降號為建威將軍。

translations.literal: At that time the Empress Dowager Kangxian held court; she was Shang’s maternal niece, and she specially ordered his demotion in rank to General Who Establishes Might.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Kangxian, Shang’s niece, was regent at the time and personally reduced him to General Who Establishes Might.

sentences.zh: 初，尚之行也，使建武將軍、濮陽太守戴施據枋頭。

translations.literal: When Shang had first set out, he had ordered Dai Shi, General Who Establishes Might and Prefect of Puyang, to hold Fangtou.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset of the campaign Shang had posted Dai Shi—General Who Establishes Might and prefect of Puyang—to Fangtou.

sentences.zh: 會冉閔之子智與其大將蔣幹來附，復遣行人劉猗詣尚請救。

translations.literal: When Ran Zhi, son of Ran Min, and his great general Jiang Gan came over to submit, he again sent the envoy Liu Yi to Shang to ask for rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Ran Min’s son Zhi and his general Jiang Gan then came over; they sent Liu Yi to beg Shang for relief.

sentences.zh: 施止猗，求傳國璽，猗歸，以告幹。

translations.literal: Shi detained Yi, demanding the Heirloom Seal; Yi returned and reported this to Gan.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Shi held Liu Yi and demanded the dynastic jade seal; Yi went back and told Jiang Gan.

sentences.zh: 幹謂尚已敗，慮不能救己，猶豫不許。

translations.literal: Gan thought Shang had already been defeated and feared he could not save himself; he hesitated and refused.
translations.idiomatic: Gan assumed Shang’s army was broken and doubted any rescue would reach Ye, so he hesitated and refused.

sentences.zh: 施遣參軍何融率壯士百入鄴，登三台助戍，譎之曰：「今且可出璽付我。

translations.literal: Shi sent his aide He Rong with a hundred stalwarts into Ye, ascending the Three Terraces to aid the garrison, and deceived him, saying: “For now you may indeed hand over the seal to me.”
translations.idiomatic: Dai Shi sent aide He Rong with a hundred picked men into Ye to reinforce the Three Terraces and lied, “Hand the seal to me for safekeeping—for now.”

sentences.zh: 凶寇在外，道路梗澀，亦未敢送璽，當遣單使馳白。

translations.literal: “The vicious raiders are outside; the roads are blocked and treacherous—we still dare not send the seal; we shall dispatch a lone rider to report swiftly.”
translations.idiomatic: “Enemy bands ring the city and the roads are choked; we dare not send the seal out yet, only a lone courier to report.”

sentences.zh: 天子聞璽已在吾許，知卿等至誠，必遣重軍相救，並厚相餉。

translations.literal: “When the Son of Heaven hears the seal is with us here, knowing your utmost sincerity he is sure to send a strong army to rescue you and will also reward you generously.”
translations.idiomatic: “Once the emperor learns the seal is safe with us, he will see your loyalty and dispatch a major relief force with rich rewards.”

sentences.zh: 」幹乃出璽付融，融齎璽馳還枋頭。

translations.literal: Gan then produced the seal and gave it to Rong; Rong carried the seal at full gallop back to Fangtou.
translations.idiomatic: Gan yielded the seal to He Rong, who galloped straight back to Fangtou with it.

sentences.zh: 尚遣振武將軍胡彬率騎三百迎璽致諸京師。

translations.literal: Shang sent Hu Bin, General Who Rouses Might, with three hundred horsemen to meet the seal and deliver it to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Shang ordered Hu Bin, General Who Rouses Might, to ride out with three hundred horsemen, take custody of the seal, and escort it to the capital.

sentences.zh: 時苻健將楊平戍許昌，尚遣兵襲破之，征授給事中，賜軺車、鼓吹，戍石頭。

translations.literal: At that time Yang Ping, a general of Fu Jian, garrisoned Xuchang; Shang sent troops to strike and rout him; Shang was summoned and appointed Palace Attendant, gifted with a light carriage and a band, and garrisoned Stone Fortress.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian’s general Yang Ping still held Xuchang; Shang smashed his garrison and was recalled as palace attendant, given a light carriage, musicians, and a posting to garrison Stone Fortress.

sentences.zh: 永和中，拜尚書僕射，出為都督江西淮南諸軍事、前將軍、豫州刺史，給事中、僕射如故，鎮曆陽，加都督豫州揚州之五郡軍事，在任有政績。

translations.literal: In the Yonghe era he was appointed Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, went out as commander of military affairs west of the river and in Huainan, Forward General, Governor of Yuzhou, while retaining Palace Attendant and Vice Director, stationed at Liyang, and was additionally given command of the military affairs of five commanderies in Yuzhou and Yangzhou; during his tenure he had administrative achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yonghe he became vice director of the secretariat, then field commander for the west-of-the-river and Huainan theaters as Forward General and governor of Yuzhou, keeping his court posts while based at Liyang; he later added five Yuzhou and Yangzhou commanderies to his brief and compiled a solid administrative record.

sentences.zh: 上表求入朝，因留京師，署僕射事。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial asking to enter court, and thus stayed in the capital, acting in Vice Director business.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized for an audience, stayed in the capital, and handled vice director duties in an acting capacity.

sentences.zh: 尋進號鎮西將軍，鎮壽陽。

translations.literal: He was shortly advanced in rank to General Who Guards the West and stationed at Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to General Who Guards the West and shifted his headquarters to Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 尚於是采拾樂人，並制石磬，以備太樂。

translations.literal: Shang thereupon gathered musicians and had stone chimes cast, to supply the Grand Music.
translations.idiomatic: Shang then recruited musicians and commissioned stone chimes to rebuild the court orchestra.

sentences.zh: 江表有鐘石之樂，自尚始也。

translations.literal: Bell-and-stone music south of the Yangzi began with Shang.
translations.idiomatic: Court music with bells and lithophones south of the Yangzi began with him.

sentences.zh: 桓溫北平洛陽，上疏請尚為都督司州諸軍事。

translations.literal: When Huan Wen pacified Luoyang on the north, he submitted a memorial asking that Shang be made commander of military affairs in Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Huan Wen took Luoyang in the north, he memorialized to put Shang in charge of all Sizhou forces.

sentences.zh: 將鎮洛陽，以疾病不行。

translations.literal: He was to have garrisoned Luoyang but, owing to illness, did not go.
translations.idiomatic: He was slated to garrison Luoyang but illness kept him from going.

sentences.zh: 升平初，又進都督豫、冀、幽、并四州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shengping he was further made commander of Yuzhou, Jizhou, Youzhou, and Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shengping his command was enlarged to cover Yuzhou, Jizhou, Youzhou, and Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 病篤，徵拜衛將軍，加散騎常侍，未至，卒于曆陽，時年五十。

translations.literal: When his illness grew grave, he was summoned as General Who Guards the Court, with additional appointment as Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary; before he arrived, he died at Liyang at the age of fifty.
translations.idiomatic: As his condition worsened he was summoned as General Who Guards the Court with cavalier attendant rank, but died at Liyang before reaching the capital, aged fifty.

sentences.zh: 詔贈散騎常侍、衛將軍、開府儀同三司，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously awarded him Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, General Who Guards the Court, and the office of equal opening to the Three Excellencies, with the posthumous title “Jian” (Simplified).
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously named him cavalier attendant, General Who Guards the Court, and ceremonially equal to the Three Excellencies, with the posthumous name “Jian” (“Unadorned”).

sentences.zh: 無子，從弟奕以子康襲爵，早卒。

translations.literal: He had no sons; his cousin Xie Yi passed his son Xie Kang to inherit the fief, but Kang died young.
translations.idiomatic: Childless, he was succeeded by his cousin Yi’s son Kang, who died young.

sentences.zh: 康弟靜復以子肅嗣，又無子。

translations.literal: Kang’s younger brother Jing again passed his son Xie Su to continue the line, and Su too had no sons.
translations.idiomatic: Kang’s brother Jing offered his own son Su as heir, but Su also left no sons.

sentences.zh: 靜子虔以子靈佑繼鯤後。

translations.literal: Jing’s son Xie Qian passed his son Lingyou to succeed Kun’s line.
translations.idiomatic: Finally Jing’s son Qian installed his boy Lingyou as heir to Xie Kun’s line.

sentences.zh: 謝安

translations.literal: Xie An.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An

sentences.zh: 謝安，字安石，尚從弟也。

translations.literal: Xie An, courtesy name Anshi, was a younger cousin of Shang.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An, courtesy name Anshi, was Shang’s younger cousin.

sentences.zh: 父裒，太常卿。

translations.literal: His father was Ai, Minister of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xie Ai served as minister of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 安年四歲時，譙郡桓彝見而歎曰：「此兒風神秀徹，後當不減王東海。

translations.literal: When An was four, Huan Yi of Qiao commandery saw him and sighed: “This child’s spirit and bearing are luminous through and through; in time he will not fall short of Wang of the Eastern Sea.”
translations.idiomatic: At four he so impressed Huan Yi of Qiao that the man exclaimed, “The clarity of this boy’s presence—one day he will stand with Wang of the Eastern Sea.”

sentences.zh: 」及總角，神識沈敏，風宇條暢，善行書。

translations.literal: When he reached the age of tying his hair, his spiritual judgment was grave and keen, his manner open and smooth, and he practiced running script well.
translations.idiomatic: By his teens his mind was steady and quick, his bearing relaxed and assured, and his running script already accomplished.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，詣王蒙，清言良久，既去，蒙子修曰：「向客何如大人？

translations.literal: At his capping he visited Wang Meng and conversed in pure talk for a long time; after he left, Meng’s son Xiu said: “How did that guest compare to you, father?”
translations.idiomatic: At his capping he spent hours in “pure conversation” with Wang Meng; when he left, Meng’s son Xiu asked, “How did that visitor measure up to you, Father?”

sentences.zh: 」蒙曰：「此客亹亹，為來逼人。

translations.literal: Meng replied: “That guest spoke unceasingly; his coming pressed one hard.”
translations.idiomatic: Meng answered, “He spoke on and on; his presence was almost overwhelming.”

sentences.zh: 」王導亦深器之。

translations.literal: Wang Dao also valued him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao esteemed him no less.

sentences.zh: 由是少有重名。

translations.literal: From this he early had heavy repute.
translations.idiomatic: From then on his reputation carried real weight while he was still young.

sentences.zh: 初辟司徒府，除佐著作郎，並以疾辭。

translations.literal: At first he was summoned to the Minister of Education’s office and appointed Assistant Editor, but both appointments he declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned first to the minister of education’s staff and named assistant editor, he pleaded illness and declined both.

sentences.zh: 寓居會稽，與王羲之及高陽許詢、桑門支遁遊處，出則漁弋山水，入則言詠屬文，無處世意。

translations.literal: He lodged at Kuaiji, roamed with Wang Xizhi, Xu Xun of Gaoyang, and the monk Zhidun; abroad they fished and hunted hills and streams, at home they conversed and composed—he had no mind to engage the world.
translations.idiomatic: He settled in Kuaiji with Wang Xizhi, Xu Xun of Gaoyang, and the monk Zhidun—fishing and roaming by day, writing and debating by night—with no interest in public life.

sentences.zh: 揚州刺史庾冰就以安有重名，必欲致之，累下郡縣敦逼，不得已赴召，月餘告歸。

translations.literal: Yu Bing, the Governor of Yangzhou, because An had heavy name was determined to get him, repeatedly ordered the commanderies and counties to press him; helplessly he answered the summons, but after little more than a month he announced he was returning home.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Yu Bing, coveting An’s fame, hounded him through every county until An grudgingly appeared—then, after barely a month, he resigned and went home.

sentences.zh: 復除尚書郎、琅邪王友，並不起。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Gentleman of the Imperial Secretariat and Companion to the Prince of Langye, but did not take either post.
translations.idiomatic: Further appointments as imperial secretary and companion to the Prince of Langye he ignored entirely.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書范汪舉安為吏部郎，安以書距絕之。

translations.literal: Fan Wang, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, recommended An for the Ministry; An sent a letter firmly refusing.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Wang, director of personnel, nominated him for a ministry post, An answered with a blunt letter of refusal.

sentences.zh: 有司奏安被召，歷年不至，禁錮終身，遂棲遲東土。

translations.literal: The relevant officials reported that An, though summoned, had not come for years; he was barred from office for life, and so he lingered in the east.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities reported his years of ignoring summons; he was blacklisted for life and remained in the eastern provinces.

sentences.zh: 嘗往臨安山中，坐石室，臨浚谷，悠然歎曰：「此去伯夷何遠！

translations.literal: He once went into the mountains at Lin’an, sat in a stone chamber overlooking a deep gorge, and sighed at leisure: “How far is this from Bo Yi!”
translations.idiomatic: Once, sitting in a stone chamber above a gorge in the Lin’an hills, he murmured, “How close this feels to Bo Yi!”

sentences.zh: 」嘗與孫綽等泛海，風起浪湧，諸人並懼，安吟嘯自若。

translations.literal: He once put to sea with Sun Chuo and others; the wind rose and waves surged; all were afraid, while An chanted and whistled as calmly as before.
translations.idiomatic: Another time he sailed with Sun Chuo and others; when a gale whipped up the waves and everyone panicked, An went on humming and whistling as if nothing had changed.

sentences.zh: 舟人以安為悅，猶去不止。

translations.literal: The boatmen thought An was enjoying it and still did not turn back.
translations.idiomatic: The crew mistook his calm for delight and held their course.

sentences.zh: 風轉急，安徐曰：「如此將何歸邪？

translations.literal: The wind grew sharper; An said slowly: “If it goes on like this, where shall we return?”
translations.idiomatic: As the storm sharpened, he said quietly, “At this rate, how do we get home?”

sentences.zh: 」舟人承言即回。

translations.literal: The boatmen took his word and at once came about.
translations.idiomatic: The boatmen took the hint and came about immediately.

sentences.zh: 眾咸服其雅量。

translations.literal: All admired his composed bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone present conceded his unflappable poise.

sentences.zh: 安雖放情丘壑，然每遊賞，必以妓女從。

translations.literal: Though An gave his heart to hills and valleys, whenever he went on an outing he always took singing girls along.
translations.idiomatic: For all his love of mountains, he never toured without a train of singing girls.

sentences.zh: 既累辟不就，簡文帝時為相，曰：「安石既與人同樂，必不得不與人同憂，召之必至。

translations.literal: Having repeatedly declined summons, when Emperor Jianwen was chief minister, the emperor said: “Anshi has shared joy with others—he cannot fail to share their cares if summoned; summon him and he will surely come.”
translations.idiomatic: After years of refusing office, Emperor Jianwen—then chief minister—remarked, “Anshi has joined others in pleasure; he cannot refuse to share their troubles. Call him and he will answer.”

sentences.zh: 」時安弟萬為西中郎將，總籓任之重。

translations.literal: At that time An’s younger brother Wan was General of the Centre of the West, bearing the weight of a frontier command.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Wan meanwhile held the critical post of General of the Centre of the West on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 安雖處衡門，其名猶出萬之右，自然有公輔之望，處家常以儀範訓子弟。

translations.literal: Though An lived behind a plain gate, his name still stood above Wan’s; naturally he carried the expectation of a ministerial post, and at home he always instructed his sons and nephews by example and rule.
translations.idiomatic: Though An lived behind a humble gate, his reputation eclipsed Wan’s; everyone expected him to reach the highest councils, and at home he drilled his kin in deportment.

sentences.zh: 安妻，劉惔妹也，既見家門富貴，而安獨靜退，乃謂曰：「丈夫不如此也？

translations.literal: An’s wife was the younger sister of Liu Dan; seeing her family enriched with honor while An alone kept aloof, she said to him: “Is this how a husband should be?”
translations.idiomatic: His wife, Liu Dan’s sister, watched the clan rise to wealth and rank while An held back and asked, “Is this what a man should do?”

sentences.zh: 」安掩鼻曰：「恐不免耳。

translations.literal: An covered his nose and said: “I fear I will not be spared in the end.”
translations.idiomatic: Pinching his nose, he muttered, “I doubt I can escape it forever.”

sentences.zh: 」及萬黜廢，安始有仕進志，時年已四十餘矣。

translations.literal: When Wan was dismissed and disgraced, An first conceived the ambition to serve; he was already over forty.
translations.idiomatic: Only after Wan’s disgrace did An think seriously of office, and he was already past forty.

sentences.zh: 征西大將軍桓溫請為司馬，將發新亭，朝士咸送，中丞高崧戲之曰：「卿累違朝旨，高臥東山，諸人每相與言，安石不肯出，將如蒼生何！

translations.literal: The Grand General Who Conquers the West, Huan Wen, invited him to be Marshal; when he was about to leave from Xinting, court gentlemen all came to see him off; Gao Song, the Palace Assistant Secretary, jested: “You have long flouted court orders and lolled on Eastern Mountain; we often said among ourselves—if Anshi will not come out, what will become of the common people!”
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen, grand general who conquers the west, named him marshal. As he was about to leave Xinting amid a throng of courtiers, Palace Assistant Secretary Gao Song teased him: “You defied every summons and lolled on Eastern Mountain while we kept asking what would become of the common people if Anshi never came out.”

sentences.zh: 蒼生今亦將如卿何！

translations.literal: “And what will become of you now that the common people turn the same question on you!”
translations.idiomatic: “And what are they to make of you now?”

sentences.zh: 」安甚有愧色。

translations.literal: An looked deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: An colored deeply with embarrassment.

sentences.zh: 既到，溫甚喜，言生平，歡笑竟日。

translations.literal: When he arrived, Wen was very pleased; they spoke of their whole lives and laughed the whole day.
translations.idiomatic: Once he arrived, Wen was delighted; they traded life stories and laughed the day away.

sentences.zh: 既出，溫問左右：「頗嘗見我有如此客不？

translations.literal: After An left, Wen asked those about him: “Have you ever seen me host a guest like that?”
translations.idiomatic: After An withdrew, Wen asked his attendants, “Have you ever seen me treat a visitor that way?”

sentences.zh: 」溫後詣安，值其理髮。

translations.literal: Later Wen called on An and found him in the middle of dressing his hair.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Wen called on An, he caught him arranging his hair.

sentences.zh: 安性遲緩，久而方罷，使取幘。

translations.literal: An by nature was slow and unhurried; only after a long while did he finish, and he had someone fetch a cap.
translations.idiomatic: An was never rushed; he took his time finishing, then sent for a cap.

sentences.zh: 溫見，留之曰：「令司馬著帽進。

translations.literal: Wen saw this and detained him, saying: “Have the Marshal enter wearing a cap.”
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen stopped him and said, “Tell the marshal to come in properly capped.”

sentences.zh: 」其見重如此。

translations.literal: Thus was he esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the regard Huan Wen showed him.

sentences.zh: 溫當北征，會萬病卒，安投箋求歸。

translations.literal: When Wen was about to campaign north, it happened that Wan died of illness; An submitted a note asking to return home.
translations.idiomatic: As Huan Wen prepared his northern expedition, Xie Wan died; An handed in a request to resign and go home.

sentences.zh: 尋除吳興太守。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed Prefect of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon named prefect of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 在官無當時譽，去後為人所思。

translations.literal: In office he had no contemporary praise, but after he left he was missed by people.
translations.idiomatic: While in post he won no loud acclaim; once he left, people remembered him fondly.

sentences.zh: 頃之徵拜侍中，遷吏部尚書、中護軍。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned as Palace Attendant, promoted to Director of the Ministry of Personnel, and Central Protector of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled as palace attendant, then rose to head the Ministry of Personnel and serve as central protector of the army.

sentences.zh: 簡文帝疾篤，溫上疏薦安宜受顧命。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jianwen was gravely ill, Wen submitted a memorial recommending that An should receive the deathbed charge.
translations.idiomatic: As Emperor Jianwen lay dying, Huan Wen memorialized that An ought to be named in the imperial testament.

sentences.zh: 及帝崩，溫入赴山陵，止新亭，大陳兵衛，將移晉室，呼安及王坦之，欲於坐害之。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, Wen entered to attend the imperial tombs, halted at Xinting, greatly arrayed armed guards, intended to shift the Jin house, summoned An and Wang Tanzhi, and wished to kill them at the seat.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor’s death Huan Wen came to the mausoleum rites, camped at Xinting with a massive escort, plotted to seize the dynasty, and called in An and Wang Tanzhi intending to murder them at the meeting.

sentences.zh: 坦之甚懼，問計于安。

translations.literal: Tanzhi was greatly afraid and asked An for a plan.
translations.idiomatic: Tanzhi was terrified and begged An for a stratagem.

sentences.zh: 安神色不變，曰：「晉祚存亡，在此一行。

translations.literal: An’s expression did not change, and he said: “The survival or fall of the Jin mandate rests on this one visit.”
translations.idiomatic: An’s face never flickered. “Whether Jin stands or falls,” he said, “rides on this interview.”

sentences.zh: 」既見溫，坦之流汗沾衣，倒執手版。

translations.literal: When they had seen Wen, Tanzhi sweated until it soaked his robes and held his memorandum tablet upside down.
translations.idiomatic: Inside, Tanzhi was drenched in sweat and clutched his name tablet upside down.

sentences.zh: 安從容就席，坐定，謂溫曰：「安聞諸侯有道，守在四鄰，明公何須壁後置人邪？

translations.literal: An calmly took his place; when seated he said to Wen: “An has heard that when the feudal lords possessed the Way, their defense lay in the four neighboring states—why must Your Excellency place men behind the screen?”
translations.idiomatic: An took his seat without hurry and told Huan Wen, “When lords upheld the Way, their bulwark was their neighbors—why post armed men behind your curtain?”

sentences.zh: 」溫笑曰：「正自不能不爾耳。

translations.literal: Wen laughed and said: “I simply could not do otherwise.”
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen smiled. “Circumstances left me no choice.”

sentences.zh: 」遂笑語移日。

translations.literal: Thereupon they laughed and conversed until the day shifted.
translations.idiomatic: They went on talking and laughing until dusk.

sentences.zh: 坦之與安初齊名，至是方知坦之之劣。

translations.literal: Tanzhi and An had at first been equally famed; only then did people realize Tanzhi’s inferiority.
translations.idiomatic: Once rivals in reputation, Tanzhi now looked plainly second-rate beside An.

sentences.zh: 溫嘗以安所作簡文帝諡議以示坐賓，曰：「此謝安石碎金也。」

translations.literal: Wen once took the posthumous-title essay for Emperor Jianwen that An had composed and showed it to the seated guests, saying: “These are shards of gold from Xie Anshi.”
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen once passed around An’s draft temple name essay for Emperor Jianwen and told the company, “Every line is a flake of gold from Xie Anshi.”

sentences.zh: 時孝武帝富於春秋，政不自己，溫威振內外，人情噂，互生同異。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Xiaowu was young in years; government was not in his own hands; Wen’s might shook inner and outer courts; human feelings murmured, and mutual agreement and division arose.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu was still a boy, real power lay elsewhere, and Huan Wen’s prestige dominated the realm—rumor ran wild and factions took shape.

sentences.zh: 安與坦之盡忠匡翼，終能輯穆。

translations.literal: An and Tanzhi exhausted loyalty in supporting and aiding, and in the end were able to bring harmony.
translations.idiomatic: An and Wang Tanzhi steadied the throne with utter loyalty until calm returned.

sentences.zh: 及溫病篤，諷朝廷加九錫，使袁宏具草。

translations.literal: When Wen was gravely ill, he hinted to the court to add the Nine Bestowals and ordered Yuan Hong to draft the text.
translations.idiomatic: As Huan Wen lay dying he pressured the court for the Nine Bestowals and told Yuan Hong to prepare the edict.

sentences.zh: 安見，輒改之，由是曆旬不就。

translations.literal: Whenever An saw it, he would alter it; for this reason it went uncompleted for weeks on end.
translations.idiomatic: An revised every draft Yuan produced, so weeks slipped by without a finished document.

sentences.zh: 會溫薨，錫命遂寢。

translations.literal: When Wen died, the bestowal edict was then shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen’s death buried the whole matter.

sentences.zh: 尋為尚書僕射，領吏部，加後將軍。

translations.literal: Shortly he became Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, heading the Ministry of Personnel, with additional rank as Rear General.
translations.idiomatic: He soon served as vice director of the secretariat while directing personnel appointments and holding the title of rear general.

sentences.zh: 及中書令王坦之出為徐州刺史，詔安總關中書事。

translations.literal: When Palace Secretariat Director Wang Tanzhi went out as Governor of Xuzhou, an edict ordered An to oversee all secretariat business.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Tanzhi left the capital for Xuzhou, An was ordered to take charge of the palace secretariat.

sentences.zh: 安義存輔導，雖會稽王道子亦賴弼諧之益。

translations.literal: An’s purpose lay in guidance and instruction; even the Prince of Kuaiji, Daozi, relied on the benefit of his support and harmony.
translations.idiomatic: An devoted himself to mentoring the throne; even Prince Daozi of Kuaiji leaned on his steadying hand.

sentences.zh: 時強敵寇境，邊書續至，梁益不守，樊鄧陷沒，安每鎮以和靖，禦以長算。

translations.literal: At that time powerful enemies raided the borders; frontier dispatches arrived in succession; Liang and Yi could not be held; Fan and Deng fell; An always steadied matters with calm and quiet, and opposed them with long-term planning.
translations.idiomatic: Enemy armies pressed the frontiers, dispatches stacked up, Liangzhou and Yizhou collapsed, Fan and Deng were lost—yet An met each crisis with unruffled calm and far-sighted strategy.

sentences.zh: 德政既行，文武用命，不存小察，弘以大綱，威懷外著，人皆比之王導，謂文雅過之。

translations.literal: Once virtuous government was practiced, civil and military obeyed orders; he did not dwell on petty scrutiny but enlarged matters with great principles; awe and cherishing showed abroad—all compared him to Wang Dao and said his culture and refinement surpassed Dao’s.
translations.idiomatic: His humane rule won obedience from every arm of government; he spurned pettifogging and set broad policy, projecting authority and grace abroad. Observers likened him to Wang Dao—some thought him the more cultivated.

sentences.zh: 嘗與王羲之登冶城，悠然遐想，有高世之志。

translations.literal: He once climbed Yecheng with Wang Xizhi, leisurely in far-reaching thought, with ambition to rise above the age.
translations.idiomatic: Once, atop the foundry hill with Wang Xizhi, he gazed into the distance with the air of a man who meant to tower above his times.

sentences.zh: 羲之謂曰：「夏禹勤王，手足胼胝；

translations.literal: Xizhi said to him: “The Great Yu toiled for the king; hands and feet were callused;
translations.idiomatic: Xizhi said, “Great Yu served the realm until his hands and feet were raw;

sentences.zh: 文王旰食，日不暇給。

translations.literal: King Wen ate at midday and evening; the days were not enough to finish his tasks.
translations.idiomatic: King Wen skipped meals; even long days were too short for his labors.

sentences.zh: 今四郊多壘，宜思自效，而虛談廢務，浮文妨要，恐非當今所宜。

translations.literal: Now the four suburbs are full of ramparts; you ought to think of devoting yourself, yet empty talk abandons affairs, and floating prose obstructs essentials—I fear this is not what the present age needs.”
translations.idiomatic: Today enemy camps ring the capital; we should throw ourselves into service, yet idle ‘pure talk’ sidelines real work and florid words block what matters—that is no fit response to our age.”

sentences.zh: 」安曰：「秦任商鞅，二世而亡，豈清言致患邪？」

translations.literal: An said: “Qin employed Shang Yang and perished in the second generation—could ‘pure talk’ have caused the calamity?”
translations.idiomatic: An answered, “Qin trusted Shang Yang and fell in two reigns—was that the fault of leisurely conversation?”

sentences.zh: 是時宮室毀壞，安欲繕之。

translations.literal: At that time the palace buildings were ruined; An wished to repair them.
translations.idiomatic: The palace lay in ruins, and An proposed rebuilding it.

sentences.zh: 尚書令王彪之等以外寇為諫，安不從，竟獨決之。

translations.literal: Director of the Imperial Secretariat Wang Biaozhi and others remonstrated citing foreign enemies; An did not follow them and in the end decided it alone.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Biaozhi and others cited foreign invasion to argue against it; An overruled them and pushed the project through on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 宮室用成，皆仰模玄象，合體辰極，而役無勞怨。

translations.literal: When the palace works were completed, all had been patterned on the celestial images and conformed to the pole of the chronograms, yet the labor levies aroused no toil or resentment.
translations.idiomatic: The new halls mirrored the constellations and aligned with the celestial pivot, yet the corvée stirred no bitterness.

sentences.zh: 又領揚州刺史，詔以甲仗百人入殿。

translations.literal: He additionally held the governorship of Yangzhou; an edict allowed him to enter the hall with a hundred men in armor.
translations.idiomatic: He added the Yangzhou governorship and was permitted to bring a hundred armed guards into the audience hall.

sentences.zh: 時帝始親萬機，進安中書監、驃騎將軍、錄尚書事，固讓軍號。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor began personally to handle the myriad threads of government; An was promoted to Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat, General of Agile Cavalry, and Recorder of Imperial Secretariat affairs, but firmly declined the military title.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor began to rule in person, An was elevated to supervise the secretariat, named general of agile cavalry, and put in charge of secretariat records—though he stubbornly refused the military rank.

sentences.zh: 于時懸象失度，亢旱彌年，安奏興滅繼絕，求晉初佐命功臣後而封之。

translations.literal: At that time the celestial signs lost their measure; severe drought stretched through the year; An submitted a memorial to restore extinguished lines and continue severed sacrifices, seeking descendants of the merit ministers who had aided the mandate at Jin’s founding and enfeoffing them.
translations.idiomatic: When drought dragged on and the heavens seemed out of joint, An memorialized to revive fallen houses and enfeoff the descendants of Jin’s founding supporters.

sentences.zh: 頃之，加司徒，後軍文武盡配大府，又讓不拜。

translations.literal: Before long he was additionally given the post of Minister of Education; the civil and military of the rear army were all assigned to the grand office; again he declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon offered the ministry of education and command of the rear army’s entire staff attached to the grand headquarters; again he refused to take office.

sentences.zh: 復加侍中、都督揚豫徐兗青五州幽州之燕國諸軍事、假節。

translations.literal: He was further given Palace Attendant, command of military affairs in Yang, Yu, Xu, Yan, and Qing five provinces and in the Yan princedom of Youzhou, and the credential staff.
translations.idiomatic: He also received palace attendant rank, command over five southern provinces plus the Yan fief in Youzhou, and the credential staff.

sentences.zh: 時苻堅強盛，疆場多虞，諸將敗退相繼。

translations.literal: At that time Fu Jian was strong and flourishing; the borders were full of alarms; the generals were defeated and retreated one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian’s power was at its height; the frontiers flared with alarms and Jin’s generals fell back in succession.

sentences.zh: 安遣弟石及兄子玄等應機征討，所在克捷。

translations.literal: An sent his younger brother Shi and his elder brother’s son Xuan and others to campaign as occasions demanded; wherever they went they achieved victory.
translations.idiomatic: An dispatched his brother Shi and nephew Xuan to meet each threat; they won wherever they fought.

sentences.zh: 拜衛將軍、開府儀同三司，封建昌縣公。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Guards the Court, with an office ceremonially equal to the Three Excellencies, and enfeoffed as Duke of Jianchang county.
translations.idiomatic: He was named General Who Guards the Court, granted an opentent equal to the Three Excellencies, and created duke of Jianchang county.

sentences.zh: 堅後率眾，號百萬，次於淮肥，京師震恐。

translations.literal: Later Jian led a host, claiming a million, and encamped along the Huai and Fei; the capital trembled with fear.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian then marched, claiming a million men, and halted along the Huai and Fei rivers, throwing the capital into panic.

sentences.zh: 加安征討大都督。

translations.literal: An was additionally given the post of grand commander for conquest.
translations.idiomatic: An was named grand commander of the expeditionary forces.

sentences.zh: 玄入問計，安夷然無懼色，答曰：「已別有旨。

translations.literal: Xuan entered to ask for a plan; An was calm and without fear, and answered: “Orders have already been issued separately.”
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan came for instructions, An showed no alarm. “The orders are already settled,” he said.

sentences.zh: 」既而寂然。

translations.literal: After that he was silent.
translations.idiomatic: Then he fell silent.

sentences.zh: 玄不敢復言，乃令張玄重請。

translations.literal: Xuan did not dare speak again and then ordered Zhang Xuan to ask again.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan dared not press further and sent Zhang Xuan to ask a second time.

sentences.zh: 安遂命駕出山墅，親朋畢集，方與玄圍棋賭別墅。

translations.literal: An thereupon ordered his carriage and went out to the mountain villa; kin and friends all gathered; only then did he play weiqi with Xuan, wagering a villa.
translations.idiomatic: An had his carriage brought to the hill estate; friends and family assembled; he sat down to a game of weiqi with Zhang Xuan, staking a villa on the outcome.

sentences.zh: 安常棋劣于于玄，是日懼，便為敵手而又不勝。

translations.literal: An was normally inferior in chess to Zhang Xuan; on that day Xuan was afraid, and they became evenly matched opponents yet [An] still did not win.
translations.idiomatic: An was usually the weaker player against Zhang Xuan, but that day fear levelled the match—yet An still could not win.

sentences.zh: 安顧謂其甥羊曇曰：「以墅乞汝。

translations.literal: An turned and said to his nephew Yang Tan: “I give you the villa.”
translations.idiomatic: He turned to his nephew Yang Tan and said, “The villa is yours.”

sentences.zh: 」安遂遊涉，至夜乃還，指授將帥，各當其任。

translations.literal: An thereupon roamed and rambled; only at night did he return, assigning the generals, each to his proper duty.
translations.idiomatic: He spent the day strolling outdoors, returned only at night, and then briefed each commander on his assignment.

sentences.zh: 玄等既破堅，有驛書至，安方對客圍棋，看書既竟，便攝放床上，了無喜色，棋如故。

translations.literal: When Xuan and the others had defeated Jian, a relay dispatch arrived; An was just playing weiqi with a guest; when he had finished reading the letter, he placed it on the bed without the least joy and continued the chess as before.
translations.idiomatic: News of Fu Jian’s defeat arrived while An entertained a guest over weiqi; he read the dispatch, set it aside without a smile, and went on with the game.

sentences.zh: 客問之，徐答云：「小兒輩遂已破賊。

translations.literal: The guest asked about it; he slowly answered: “The young fellows have already routed the bandits.”
translations.idiomatic: When the guest asked, he said quietly, “The boys have already broken the enemy.”

sentences.zh: 」既罷，還內，過戶限，心喜甚，不覺屐齒之折，其矯情鎮物如此。

translations.literal: When it was over, he returned within; crossing the door sill, his heart rejoiced extremely, and without noticing he broke the teeth of his clogs—thus did he feign composure to steady others.
translations.idiomatic: Inside, crossing the threshold, he was so elated that he snapped the pegs of his clogs without noticing—such was his habit of masking emotion to steady those around him.

sentences.zh: 以總統功，進拜太保。

translations.literal: By merit of overall command he was advanced and appointed Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: For supreme command of the victory he was promoted to grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 安方欲混一文軌，上疏求自北征，乃進都督揚、江、荊、司、豫、徐、兗、青、冀、幽、并、寧、益、雍、梁十五州軍事，加黃鉞，其本官如故，置從事中郎二人。

translations.literal: An was about to unify writing and cart tracks; he submitted a memorial asking to campaign north in person; he was then advanced to command the military affairs of fifteen provinces—Yang, Jiang, Jing, Si, Yu, Xu, Yan, Qing, Ji, You, Bing, Ning, Yi, Yong, and Liang—with the golden battle-ax, his original offices remaining as before, and two staff advisers were appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Intent on reunifying the realm, An asked to lead the northern expedition himself and received command over fifteen provinces, the golden axe, retention of his existing posts, and two senior staff appointments.

sentences.zh: 安上疏讓太保及爵，不許。

translations.literal: An submitted a memorial declining the Grand Tutorship and the noble rank; it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to refuse the grand tutorship and ducal title; the throne would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 是時桓沖既卒，荊、江二州並缺，物論以玄勳望，宜以授之。

translations.literal: At that time Huan Chong had died; Jing and Jiang provinces were both vacant; public opinion, by Xuan’s merit and standing, held that they should be given to him.
translations.idiomatic: With Huan Chong dead and both Jingzhou and Jiangzhou open, opinion favored giving them to Xuan on the strength of his record and prestige.

sentences.zh: 安以父子皆著大勳，恐為朝廷所疑，又懼桓氏失職，桓石虔復有沔陽之功，慮其驍猛，在形勝之地，終或難制，乃以桓石民為荊州，改桓伊于中流，石虔為豫州。

translations.literal: An, because father and son had both earned great merit, feared suspicion from the court; he also feared the Huan clan losing office; Huan Shiquan again had merit at Mianyang; he worried about his fierce valor—in a strategically strong place he might in the end be hard to control—therefore he made Huan Shimin Jingzhou, transferred Huan Yi to the midstream, and Shiquan to Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An worried that handing both posts to the Xuan branch—already laden with honors—would alarm the court, while leaving the Huans empty-handed might backfire: Huan Shiquan’s ferocity and victory at Mianyang made him dangerous on critical ground. He split the prize, giving Jingzhou to Huan Shimin, the river defense to Huan Yi, and Yuzhou to Shiquan.

sentences.zh: 既以三桓據三州，彼此無恐，各得所任。

translations.literal: Once the three Huans held three provinces, neither side feared the other, and each obtained a fitting assignment.
translations.idiomatic: With three Huans on three provinces, the clan was satisfied and the throne unthreatened—each man had a fitting charge.

sentences.zh: 其經遠無競，類皆如此。

translations.literal: His farsighted lack of contention was in kind all like this.
translations.idiomatic: His long-sighted, ungrudging settlements usually looked like this.

sentences.zh: 性好音樂，自弟萬喪，十年不聽音樂。

translations.literal: He was fond of music by nature; from his younger brother Wan’s death, for ten years he did not listen to music.
translations.idiomatic: He loved music, yet for ten years after Wan’s death he would not hear a note.

sentences.zh: 及登臺輔，期喪不廢樂。

translations.literal: When he ascended to the highest ministers, he did not abandon music during the one-year mourning period.
translations.idiomatic: Once he reached the summit of power, he kept musicians even during lesser mourning.

sentences.zh: 王坦之書喻之，不從，衣冠效之，遂以成俗。

translations.literal: Wang Tanzhi wrote to instruct him; he did not comply; officials followed his example, and it thus became custom.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tanzhi wrote to protest; An ignored him, and the gentry imitated him until the practice spread.

sentences.zh: 又于土山營墅，樓館林竹甚盛，每攜中外子侄往來游集，肴饌亦屢費百金，世頗以此譏焉，而安殊不以屑意。

translations.literal: He also built a villa on the earthen hill; towers, lodges, woods, and bamboo were very luxuriant; he often brought inner and outer sons and nephews back and forth to roam and gather, and viands repeatedly cost a hundred in gold; the age rather ridiculed him for this, yet An did not regard it as worth a thought.
translations.idiomatic: He raised a lavish villa on the artificial hill, hosting kinsmen with feasts that sometimes cost a hundred ounces of gold; contemporaries ridiculed him, but An brushed it off.

sentences.zh: 常疑劉牢之既不可獨任，又知王味之不宜專城。

translations.literal: He always doubted that Liu Laozhi could bear sole responsibility, and also knew that Wang Weizhi was not fit to hold a city alone.
translations.idiomatic: He long doubted Liu Laozhi could safely hold sole command and knew Wang Weizhi was wrong to govern a strategic city alone.

sentences.zh: 牢之既以亂終，而味之亦以貪敗，由是識者服其知人。

translations.literal: Laozhi in the end met disorder, and Weizhi also failed through greed; for this reason those who discerned admired his knowledge of men.
translations.idiomatic: Laozhi ended in mutiny and Weizhi fell to corruption—observers then conceded An’s eye for character.

sentences.zh: 時會稽王道子專權，而奸諂頗相扇構，安出鎮廣陵之步丘，築壘曰新城以避之。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Kuaiji, Daozi, monopolized power, and wicked flatterers fanned intrigues; An went out to garrison Buchou in Guangling and built a rampart called New City to avoid them.
translations.idiomatic: With Prince Daozi of Kuaiji wielding power and sycophants weaving plots, An took up headquarters at Buchou in Guangling and threw up “New City” to keep his distance.

sentences.zh: 帝出祖于西池，獻觴賦詩焉。

translations.literal: The emperor went out to perform the road sacrifice at West Pool and presented cups and composed poems.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw him off at West Pool with wine and verse.

sentences.zh: 安雖受朝寄，然東山之志始末不渝，每形於言色。

translations.literal: Although An received the court’s charge, yet his Eastern Mountain resolve from first to last did not change, and it often showed in word and expression.
translations.idiomatic: Despite shouldering state business, he never renounced his dream of returning to Eastern Mountain; it showed in every word and glance.

sentences.zh: 及鎮新城，盡室而行，造泛海之裝，欲須經略粗定，自江道還東。

translations.literal: When he garrisoned New City, he moved the whole household, prepared gear for putting to sea, and intended, once planning was roughly settled, to return east by the river route.
translations.idiomatic: At New City he moved his entire household and fitted out a seagoing return, planning to slip back east by river once the frontier was stable.

sentences.zh: 雅志未就，遂遇疾篤。

translations.literal: His lofty ambition was not achieved, and he then encountered grave illness.
translations.idiomatic: That dream went unfulfilled; grave illness struck first.

sentences.zh: 上疏請量宜旋旆，並召子征虜將軍琰解甲息徒，命龍驤將軍硃序進據洛陽，前鋒都督玄抗威彭沛，委以董督。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial asking to measure the situation and turn the banners homeward, and simultaneously summoned his son Yan, General Who Conquers the Barbarians, to lay down armor and rest the troops, ordered Zhu Xu, General Who Dragons His Banner, to advance and hold Luoyang, and the vanguard commander Xuan to display might at Peng and Pei, entrusting them with overall supervision.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized for a prudent withdrawal, told his son Yan to stand the army down, ordered Zhu Xu toward Luoyang and Xuan to hold the Peng–Pei front, charging them with overall direction.

sentences.zh: 若二賊假延，來年水生，東西齊舉。

translations.literal: If the two bandits borrow delay, when next year the waters rise, east and west will strike together.
translations.idiomatic: If both enemies linger, we would strike east and west together when the spring floods come.

sentences.zh: 詔遣侍中慰勞，遂還都。

translations.literal: An edict sent a Palace Attendant to console and reward, and he then returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent a palace attendant to console him, and he came back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 聞當輿入西州門，自以本志不遂，深自慨失，因悵然謂所親曰：「昔桓溫在時，吾常懼不全。

translations.literal: Hearing that he was to be carried in through the West Province Gate, he considered that his original ambition was not fulfilled, deeply felt loss in himself, and therefore said sadly to those close: “In the past when Huan Wen was alive, I always feared I would not survive intact.”
translations.idiomatic: Learning his litter would pass the West Province gate, he brooded that his lifelong wish had failed and said to intimates, “When Huan Wen lived, I always feared I might not survive.”

sentences.zh: 忽夢乘溫輿行十六里，見一白雞而止。

translations.literal: Suddenly he dreamed of riding in Wen’s litter for sixteen li and stopping when he saw a white rooster.
translations.idiomatic: He dreamed he rode Huan Wen’s carriage sixteen li and halted at a white cockerel.

sentences.zh: 乘溫輿者，代其位也。

translations.literal: Riding Wen’s litter means succeeding to his place.
translations.idiomatic: The carriage meant another had taken Huan Wen’s seat.

sentences.zh: 十六里，止今十六年矣。

translations.literal: Sixteen li means stopping at the present sixteen years.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen li stood for sixteen years—now complete.

sentences.zh: 白雞主酉，今太歲在酉，吾病殆不起乎！

translations.literal: The white rooster governs the you hour; now the Grand Year is in you; my illness is perhaps about not rising!”
translations.idiomatic: White fowl marks the you hour; the year-star sits in you—this illness will kill me!”

sentences.zh: 」乃上疏遜位，詔遣侍中、尚書喻旨。

translations.literal: He then submitted a memorial yielding office; an edict sent a Palace Attendant and the Imperial Secretariat to convey the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to retire; the throne answered through a palace attendant and secretariat officials.

sentences.zh: 先是，安發石頭，金鼓忽破，又語未嘗謬，而忽一誤，眾亦怪異之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when An set out from Stone Fortress, the gongs and drums suddenly broke; moreover his speech had never erred, yet suddenly he made one mistake—the crowd also thought it strange.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, leaving Stone Fortress, his drums had snapped mid-march; he, never wrong in speech, once misspoke—onlookers took both for omens.

sentences.zh: 尋薨，時年六十六。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he died, aged sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after, at sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 帝三日臨於朝堂，賜東園秘器、朝服一具、衣一襲、錢百萬、布千匹、蠟五百斤，贈太傅，諡曰文靖。

translations.literal: The emperor for three days attended mourning in the court hall; he was granted secret funeral gear from the Eastern Park, one set of court dress, one suit of clothes, a million cash, a thousand bolts of cloth, five hundred jin of wax; he was posthumously awarded Grand Tutor with the posthumous title “Wenjing” (Cultured and Tranquil).
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him three days in court, heaped gifts of coffin finery, robes, cash, cloth, and wax upon his house, and posthumously named him grand tutor with the epithet Wenjing, “Cultured and Serene.”

sentences.zh: 以無下舍，詔府中備凶儀。

translations.literal: Because there was no lower residence, an edict ordered the office to prepare funeral rites.
translations.idiomatic: He had no town house, so the court ordered the ministry to stage the obsequies.

sentences.zh: 及葬，加殊禮，依大司馬桓溫故事。

translations.literal: When he was buried, extraordinary rites were added, following the precedent of Grand Marshal Huan Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Burial honors matched those once given Grand Marshal Huan Wen.

sentences.zh: 又以平苻堅勳，更封廬陵郡公。

translations.literal: Again, by merit of pacifying Fu Jian, he was further enfeoffed as Duke of Luling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: For the victory over Fu Jian his fief was raised to duke of Luling commandery.

sentences.zh: 安少有盛名，時多愛慕。

translations.literal: An from youth had great fame; many of the age admired him.
translations.idiomatic: From youth his fame drew wide admiration.

sentences.zh: 鄉人有罷中宿縣者，還詣安。

translations.literal: A fellow townsman who had been dismissed from Zhongsu county returned to visit An.
translations.idiomatic: A countryman back from a stint at Zhongsu county called on him.

sentences.zh: 安問其歸資，答曰：「有蒲葵扇五萬。

translations.literal: An asked about his travel funds for returning; he answered: “I have fifty thousand palm-leaf fans.”
translations.idiomatic: An asked what he had brought home. “Fifty thousand palm-leaf fans,” said the man.

sentences.zh: 」安乃取其中者捉之，京師士庶競市，價增數倍。

translations.literal: An then took one of the middling sort and held it; gentlemen and commoners of the capital vied to buy, and the price rose several fold.
translations.idiomatic: An picked an average fan to carry; the capital mobbed the market and prices multiplied.

sentences.zh: 安本能為洛下書生詠，有鼻疾，故其音濁，名流愛其詠而弗能及，或手掩鼻以斅之。

translations.literal: An by nature could perform the Luoyang scholars’ chant; he had a nasal ailment, so his tone was thick; eminent men loved his chant but could not match it; some covered their noses with their hands to imitate it.
translations.idiomatic: He sang the Luoyang scholar’s tune in a muffled voice—his chronic nasal trouble—and leading men adored the sound yet could only mimic it by pinching their noses.

sentences.zh: 及至新城，築埭於城北，後人追思之，名為召伯埭。

translations.literal: When he reached New City, he built a dike north of the city; later people recalled him and named it the Duke of Shao Dike.
translations.idiomatic: At New City he raised a northward dike later named for the Duke of Shao in his honor.

translations.literal: An equals sign printed alone in the received text as a layout divider.

sentences.zh: 附 羊曇

translations.literal: Supplement: Yang Tan.
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Yang Tan

translations.literal: An equals sign printed alone in the received text as a layout divider.

sentences.zh: 羊曇者，太山人，知名士也，為安所愛重。

translations.literal: Yang Tan was a man of Taishan, a renowned scholar, whom An loved and esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Tan of Taishan was a celebrated scholar whom An cherished.

sentences.zh: 安薨後，輟樂彌年，行不由西州路。

translations.literal: After An died, he ceased music for a full year and did not travel by the West Province road.
translations.idiomatic: After An’s death he gave up music for a year and would not walk the West Province road.

sentences.zh: 嘗因石頭大醉，扶路唱樂，不覺至州門。

translations.literal: Once because of great drunkenness at Stone Fortress he leaned on the road singing music, and without noticing arrived at the province gate.
translations.idiomatic: Once, staggering drunk from Stone Fortress, he sang his way along until he found himself at the province gate.

sentences.zh: 左右白曰：「此西州門。

translations.literal: Those about him said: “This is the West Province Gate.”
translations.idiomatic: His attendants told him, “This is the West Province gate.”

sentences.zh: 」曇悲感不已，以馬策扣扉，誦曹子建詩曰：「生存華屋處，零落歸山丘。

translations.literal: Tan, grief-stricken without end, beat the door with his riding crop and recited Cao Zijian’s poem: “While alive you dwelt in splendid halls; scattered, you return to the hillock.”
translations.idiomatic: Overcome, Tan thrashed the gate with his whip and chanted Cao Zhi’s lines about glory in life and dust in death.

sentences.zh: 」慟哭而去。

translations.literal: Wailing bitterly, he left.
translations.idiomatic: He wept his way off.

sentences.zh: 安有二子：瑤、琰。

translations.literal: An had two sons: Yao and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An left two sons, Yao and Yan.

translations.literal: An equals sign printed alone in the received text as a layout divider.

sentences.zh: 安子 瑤

translations.literal: An’s son: Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An’s son: Yao

translations.literal: An equals sign printed alone in the received text as a layout divider.

sentences.zh: 瑤襲爵，官至琅邪王友，早卒。

translations.literal: Yao inherited the noble rank; his office reached Companion to the Prince of Langye; he died young.
translations.idiomatic: Yao succeeded to the title, rose to companion to the prince of Langye, and died young.

sentences.zh: 子該嗣，終東陽太守。

translations.literal: His son Gai succeeded; he ended as Prefect of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gai inherited the fief and finished his career as prefect of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 無子，弟光祿勳模以子承伯嗣，有罪，國除。

translations.literal: Having no sons, his younger brother Mo, Supervisor of the Office of the Imperial Clan, passed his son Chengbo to continue the line; there was a crime, and the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Without an heir, his uncle Mo, supervisor of the imperial clan, offered son Chengbo; a crime followed and the marquisate was stripped.

sentences.zh: 劉裕以安勳德濟世，特更封該弟澹為柴桑侯，邑千戶，奉安祀。

translations.literal: Liu Yu, because An’s merit and virtue had aided the age, specially again enfeoffed Gai’s younger brother Dan as Marquis of Chaisang, with a fief of a thousand households, to maintain An’s sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu, honoring An’s service to the realm, created Dan—Gai’s brother—marquis of Chaisang with a thousand households to tend An’s rites.

sentences.zh: 澹少曆顯位，桓玄篡位，以澹兼太尉，與王謐俱齎冊到姑孰。

translations.literal: Dan from youth had held prominent posts; when Huan Xuan usurped the throne, he made Dan concurrently Grand Commandant and, with Wang Mi, together carried the abdication documents to Gushu.
translations.idiomatic: Dan had long held high office; under Huan Xuan’s usurpation he served as grand commandant and, with Wang Mi, delivered the accession tablets to Gushu.

sentences.zh: 元熙中，為光祿大夫，復兼太保，持節奉冊禪宋。

translations.literal: In the Yuanxi era he was Palace Counsellor, again concurrently Grand Tutor, holding the staff to present the abdication register in yielding Song.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yuanxi he was palace counsellor and again titular grand tutor, bearing the staff to hand over the Jin abdication to Song.

translations.literal: An equals sign printed alone in the received text as a layout divider.

sentences.zh: 安子 琰

translations.literal: An’s son: Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An’s son: Yan

translations.literal: An equals sign printed alone in the received text as a layout divider.

sentences.zh: 琰字瑗度。

translations.literal: Yan, courtesy name Yuandu.
translations.idiomatic: Yan’s courtesy name was Yuandu.

sentences.zh: 弱冠以貞幹稱，美風姿。

translations.literal: At his capping he was praised for chaste competence; his bearing was handsome.
translations.idiomatic: Capped young, he was known for integrity and ability, and he cut a striking figure.

sentences.zh: 與從兄護軍淡雖比居，不往來，宗中子弟惟與才令者數人相接。

translations.literal: With his elder cousin, the Protector Dan, though they lived next to each other, they did not visit back and forth; among the clan’s younger kin he associated with only a few who had talent and poise.
translations.idiomatic: He lived beside his cousin Dan, the protector, yet they rarely met; among kinsmen he kept company only with the most gifted.

sentences.zh: 拜著作郎，轉秘書丞，累遷散騎常侍、侍中。

translations.literal: He was appointed Editor, transferred to Assistant Director of the Palace Library, and by stages promoted to Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from editor to assistant director of the palace library, then to cavalier attendant and palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 苻堅之役，安以琰有軍國才用，出為輔國將軍，以精卒八千，與從兄玄俱陷陣破堅，以勳封望蔡公，尋遭父憂去官，服闋，除征虜將軍、會稽內史。

translations.literal: In the Fu Jian campaign, An, because Yan had talent for military and state affairs, sent him out as General Who Supports the State with eight thousand picked troops; with his elder cousin Xuan he together broke the enemy line and defeated Jian; by merit he was enfeoffed as Duke of Wangcai, then encountered his father’s bereavement and left office; when mourning ended, he was appointed General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Interior Minister of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: At Fei River, An judged Yan fit for war and statecraft, gave him eight thousand elite troops as General Who Supports the State, and watched him shatter Fu Jian’s line beside cousin Xuan—merit that earned the duchy of Wangcai. Mourning for his father interrupted service; afterward he became General Who Conquers the Barbarians and interior minister of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 頃之。

translations.literal: Before long.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after.

sentences.zh: 徵為尚書右僕射，領太子詹事，加散騎常侍，將軍如故。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, heading the heir apparent’s household office, with additional Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, while remaining General as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as right vice director of the secretariat and supervisor of the heir apparent’s household, kept his general’s commission, and added cavalier attendant.

sentences.zh: 又遭母憂，朝廷疑其葬禮。

translations.literal: Again he suffered his mother’s bereavement; the court was uncertain about his funeral observances.
translations.idiomatic: His mother’s death left the court debating how his mourning rites should run.

sentences.zh: 時議者云：「潘岳為賈充婦《宜城宣君誄》云：'昔在武侯，喪禮殊倫。

translations.literal: Debaters said: “In Pan Yue’s dirge for Lady Xuan of Yicheng, wife of Jia Chong, it says: ‘Formerly at the Marquis of Wu, mourning rites were special in kind.’
translations.idiomatic: Counselors cited Pan Yue’s dirge for Jia Chong’s wife: ‘At the house of the Wu marquis, mourning broke the usual mold.’

sentences.zh: 伉儷一體，朝儀則均。

translations.literal: ‘Husband and wife are one body; court ritual should be equal.’
translations.idiomatic: ‘Spouses are one; court ceremony should treat them alike.’

sentences.zh: '謂宜資給葬，悉依太傅故事。

translations.literal: ‘—meaning supplies for the funeral should be provided, all following the precedent of the Grand Tutor.’
translations.idiomatic: ‘So the state should fund the burial on the model used for the grand tutor.’

sentences.zh: 」先是，王珣娶萬女，珣弟瑉娶安女，並不終，由是與謝氏有隙。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wang Xun had married Wan’s daughter, Xun’s younger brother Min had married An’s daughter, and neither marriage lasted to the end; for this [the Wangs] had a rift with the Xies.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xun had wed Wan’s daughter and his brother Min had wed An’s daughter—both unions failed—so the Wangs nursed a grudge against the Xies.

sentences.zh: 珣時為僕射，猶以前憾緩其事。

translations.literal: Xun at that time was Vice Director; still bearing the old grudge, he delayed the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Xun, now vice director, dragged his feet out of spite.

sentences.zh: 琰聞恥之，遂自造轀輬車以葬，議者譏之。

translations.literal: Yan, hearing this, felt shamed and thereupon had a hearselike carriage made himself for the burial; debaters ridiculed him.
translations.idiomatic: Humiliated, Yan built his own funeral wagon; critics sneered.

sentences.zh: 太元末，為護軍將軍，加右將軍。

translations.literal: In the last years of Taiyuan he was General Who Guards the Army, with additional rank as General of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Taiyuan he was General Who Guards the Army with concurrent rank as general of the right.

sentences.zh: 會稽王道子以為司馬，右將軍如故。

translations.literal: The Prince of Kuaiji, Daozi, made him Marshal, while he remained General of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Daozi of Kuaiji named him marshal while he kept the right general’s baton.

sentences.zh: 王恭舉兵，假琰節，都督前鋒軍事。

translations.literal: When Wang Gong raised troops, Yan was given the credential staff and commanded the vanguard army.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong’s revolt earned Yan the credential staff and command of the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 恭平，遷衛將軍、徐州刺史、假節。

translations.literal: When Gong was pacified, he was promoted to General Who Guards the Court, Governor of Xuzhou, with credential staff.
translations.idiomatic: After Gong’s defeat he became General Who Guards the Court and governor of Xuzhou, still bearing the staff.

sentences.zh: 孫恩作亂，加督吳興、義興二郡軍事，討恩。

translations.literal: When Sun En rebelled, he was additionally put in command of military affairs in Wuxing and Yixing, to campaign against En.
translations.idiomatic: Sun En’s rising added command of Wuxing and Yixing to his brief.

sentences.zh: 至義興，斬賊許允之，迎太守魏鄢還郡。

translations.literal: Reaching Yixing, he beheaded the bandit Xu Yunzhi and escorted Prefect Wei Yan back to the command.
translations.idiomatic: In Yixing he executed the rebel Xu Yunzhi and restored Prefect Wei Yan to his yamen.

sentences.zh: 進討吳興賊丘尪，破之。

translations.literal: He advanced to attack the bandit Qiu Gang of Wuxing and routed him.
translations.idiomatic: He marched on Wuxing and crushed Qiu Gang’s band.

sentences.zh: 又詔琰與輔國將軍劉牢之俱討孫恩。

translations.literal: Again an edict ordered Yan and Liu Laozhi, General Who Supports the State, jointly to campaign against Sun En.
translations.idiomatic: The court paired him with Liu Laozhi, General Who Supports the State, for a second strike at Sun En.

sentences.zh: 恩逃於海島，朝廷憂之，以琰為會稽內史、都督五郡軍事，本官並如故。

translations.literal: En fled to a sea island; the court worried and made Yan Interior Minister of Kuaiji, commander of military affairs in five commanderies, his original posts all as before.
translations.idiomatic: En slipped offshore; alarmed, the court made Yan interior minister of Kuaiji with five commanderies under his command, leaving his other titles intact.

sentences.zh: 琰既以資望鎮越土，議者謂無復東顧之虞。

translations.literal: Since Yan by seniority and repute held Yue lands, debaters said there was no further anxiety of looking east.
translations.idiomatic: His prestige was thought enough to secure the entire southeast.

sentences.zh: 及至郡，無綏撫之能，而不為武備。

translations.literal: When he reached the commandery, he had no ability to console and rule, yet made no military preparations.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he neither soothed the people nor readied defenses.

sentences.zh: 將帥皆諫曰：「強賊在海，伺人形便，宜振揚仁風，開其自新之路。

translations.literal: His generals all remonstrated: “The fierce bandits are at sea, watching for human openings; you should raise benevolent influence and open a road for them to renew themselves.”
translations.idiomatic: His officers urged, ‘The raiders lurk offshore waiting for a slip; show mercy and offer them a way back.’

sentences.zh: 」琰曰：「苻堅百萬，尚送死淮南，況孫恩奔衄歸海，何能復出！

translations.literal: Yan said: “Fu Jian’s million still came to die south of the Huai—how much more Sun En, routed and fleeing to the sea—how could he come out again!”
translations.idiomatic: Yan replied, ‘Fu Jian’s million died south of the Huai—Sun En is a beaten refugee at sea; he cannot return!’

sentences.zh: 若其復至，正是天不養國賊，令速就戮耳。

translations.literal: ‘If he does return, that is simply Heaven not nurturing the traitors of the state, making them quickly submit to execution.’
translations.idiomatic: ‘If he does, Heaven itself has turned on the traitors and will deliver them to the blade.’

sentences.zh: 」遂不從其言。

translations.literal: Thereupon he did not follow their words.
translations.idiomatic: He ignored the advice.

sentences.zh: 恩後果復寇浹口，入余姚，破上虞，進及邢浦，去山陰北三十五里。

translations.literal: En afterward indeed again raided Jia Estuary, entered Yuyao, broke Shangyu, and advanced to Xingpu, thirty-five li north of Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: Sun En struck Jia Estuary, took Yuyao and Shangyu, and pushed to Xingpu, thirty-five li north of Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 琰遣參軍劉宣之距破恩。

translations.literal: Yan sent his aide Liu Xuanzhi to resist and rout En.
translations.idiomatic: Yan dispatched aide Liu Xuanzhi, who drove him back.

sentences.zh: 既而上党太守張虔碩戰敗，群賊銳進，人情震駭，咸以宜持重嚴備，且列水軍于南湖，分兵設伏以待之。

translations.literal: Presently Shangdang Prefect Zhang Qianshuo was defeated in battle; the mass of bandits pressed sharply forward; human hearts were shocked; all said heavy defense should be maintained and a water force arrayed on South Lake, dividing troops to set ambushes and await them.
translations.idiomatic: Then Zhang Qianshuo of Shangdang lost a fight; the rebels surged; panic spread; advisors called for a cautious stand, a fleet on South Lake, and ambushes along the approach.

sentences.zh: 琰不聽。

translations.literal: Yan did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Yan refused.

sentences.zh: 賊既至，尚未食，琰曰：「要當先滅此寇而後食也。

translations.literal: When the bandits arrived, [Yan] had not yet eaten; Yan said: “We must first destroy this banditry and then eat.”
translations.idiomatic: The enemy appeared before Yan had eaten; he declared, ‘We dine only after we crush them.’

sentences.zh: 」跨馬而出。

translations.literal: He mounted his horse and went out.
translations.idiomatic: He vaulted into the saddle and rode out.

sentences.zh: 廣武將軍桓寶為前鋒，摧鋒陷陣，殺賊甚多，而塘路迮狹，琰軍魚貫而前，賊於艦中傍射之，前後斷絕。

translations.literal: Huan Bao, General Who Extends Might, was vanguard, crushing the front line and piercing the formation, killing many bandits, but the dyke road was narrow and Yan’s army filed forward in a line; the bandits shot from the side of their ships; front and rear were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Bao’s vanguard tore deep into the rebels, but the embankment was narrow—Yan’s men strung out in single file while ships raked them from the flanks and cut the column in two.

sentences.zh: 琰至千秋亭，敗績。

translations.literal: Yan reached Qianqiu Pavilion and met a crushing defeat.
translations.idiomatic: At Qianqiu Pavilion his line collapsed.

sentences.zh: 琰帳下都督張猛于後斫琰馬，琰墮地，與二子肇、峻俱被害，寶亦死之。

translations.literal: Zhang Meng, a camp commander under Yan, from behind hacked Yan’s horse; Yan fell to the ground, and together with his two sons Zhao and Jun was killed; Bao also died.
translations.idiomatic: Yan’s camp officer Zhang Meng hacked his mount from behind; Yan fell and died with his sons Zhao and Jun; Bao perished too.

sentences.zh: 後劉裕左裏之捷，生擒猛，送琰小子混，混刳肝生食之。
